solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One way ticket put on credit card, our grandkids'll pay for it!

indicators.note: on says the earlier pieces come before the card piece in sequence

parts.note: a one-way rail ticket is called a single in Britain
to put something to work is to employ or apply it
plastic is everyday slang for a credit or debit card

explanation.surface: Someone buys a one-way ticket on credit, grumbling that the next generation will foot the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE is the British name for a one-way ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwaway synthetic items pollute for centuries, so later generations bear the environmental cost: the clue's exclamation is a cryptic gloss rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Special beers a feature of Boxing Day?

parts.note: ales are beers

explanation.surface: Drinking special beers is part of the Boxing Day celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing Day, 26 December, is a British public holiday famous for shops' big discount events.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers in Britain traditionally launch their big price-cut events on the day after Christmas, so this is an example-style definition.

clue.text: Not a vintage Welsh town

parts.note: read with what follows, not vintage means new, the opposite of aged
a vintage is a fine aged fortified wine, as in vintage port

explanation.surface: A Welsh town is said to have no vintage to boast of.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a young wine; the setter splits it, so 'Not' does double work as the opposite of vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: A city and former town in south-east Wales, at the mouth of the Usk, named literally.

clue.text: Doctor run over visiting royal flipping dignitary

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole assembly back to front
visiting puts the doctor, run and over pieces inside the royal word, like a guest in a house

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A doctor runs over a royal visitor who is having a tantrum, flipping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses the whole assembly, ROYAMDROL, so the doctor's letters read DM in the grid. O for over is cricket shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic head of a major city such as London is an official of high rank, so a type of dignitary.

clue.text: Some launder these articles when in U-boat

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A laundry instruction: wash some of these articles while you are on the submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine travels below the ocean's surface, so a crew aboard one are beneath the waves.

clue.text: Victim of fungus regularly exhibited red lump

indicators.note: regularly exhibited says every other letter of red lump is shown, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A fungal infection shows up as a red lump.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch elm disease, a fungus spread by beetles, killed most of Britain's elms in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree species was devastated by a fungal disease, making it a famous casualty of one.

clue.text: Leading artist — Constable perhaps — gets a source of oil

indicators.note: Leading says the police piece goes in front of the artist piece

parts.note: a constable is a police officer, a cop; the capital hides the sense
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A leading painter such as John Constable is credited as a source of oil paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like the painter John Constable but means a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried coconut kernel is pressed to yield coconut oil, so it is literally a raw material for oil.

clue.text: A piece of cake for top military bod Henry

parts.note: C-in-C is the Commander-in-Chief, the top military person
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A slice of cake is offered to a senior officer called Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for something very easy to do.

clue.text: See 1 across
A northern Arab state is replacing King with son — that's a relief!

indicators.note: is replacing says one letter of the state's name gives way to another

parts.note: Algeria is an Arab country in North Africa
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A northern Arab country changing its monarch for his son brings relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing King with son' swaps the R of ALGERIA for S, giving ALGESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term is for absence of pain, which is literally relief from suffering.

clue.text: Threatened junior journalist

parts.note: a junior rank is a lower one
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A junior reporter has been threatened.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the old verb lour, also spelt lower: to look dark and menacing, as a sky does.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the sky or a face, looked dark and menacing, an old verb related to frowning.

clue.text: Universal symbol not unknown in Kipling's work

indicators.note: not says the unknown letter is left out

parts.note: Mandalay is a poem by Rudyard Kipling
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A literary critic finds a universal symbol in Kipling's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist art the circular design represents the cosmos, so it is a symbol of the universe.

clue.text: X-Men character ripped end off S&M clothing

indicators.note: clothing says the outer letters wrap around the middle piece

parts.note: taken as its two capitals

indicators.note: end off says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ripped means torn

explanation.surface: A comic-book heroine has torn the end off her bondage outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like the garments in the surface but means wrapping around.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather-controlling mutant heroine in Marvel's superhero team, played on film by Halle Berry.

clue.text: Wealthy stock speculator hedging European parliament

indicators.note: hedging means surrounding, like a hedge round a field

parts.note: wealthy means rich
a stag buys new share issues to sell quickly at a profit

explanation.surface: A rich investor hedges his bets against a European parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedging' looks like the financial sense of offsetting risk but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berlin building houses Germany's federal legislature, so it stands for that assembly.

clue.text: Ugly Soviet row about vacant ritzy housing for the out-of-touch elite?

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go round the empty ritzy piece
ugly suggests the letters are twisted out of shape
vacant says ritzy loses its inside, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: An ugly Soviet block is rebuilt as luxury housing for the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ugly' scrambles SOVIET ROW into IVOTOWERS, which is split by RY, the shell of 'ritzy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a retreat of academics or intellectuals detached from practical life, pictured as a building they live in.

clue.text: Wife leaving a hint of perfume behind

indicators.note: leaving says the wife's letter departs

parts.note: a waft is a faint whiff of scent

explanation.surface: A departing wife leaves a trace of her scent behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like part of the surface's scent trail but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for the rear of a ship, meaning towards the back.

clue.text: A FT column, a new article for those in the 12, and a great leader!

parts.note: Lex is the Financial Times's daily business commentary column
der is a German definite article, used by those in the Reichstag at 12 across

explanation.surface: A newspaper column profiles an article on a great leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 is the answer at 12 across, the German parliament, so its members' article is German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian king who conquered the Persian Empire is known as 'the Great', an example of a famous commander.

clue.text: Oh Okay; Boy Scouts upset by universal insult

indicators.note: by says the universal letter sits beside the scrambled ones, at the end
upset means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Boy Scouts, upset, hurl a universally understood insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Mostly British schoolyard jeering, said to dismiss someone with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish exclamation of derision, a jeer used as a playground taunt.

clue.text: Thai temple pews turned up a year after having been taken by storm surge

definitions.text: having been taken by storm surge

indicators.note: after says the year piece follows the reversed letters
turned up in a down clue says the temple and pews are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand

explanation.surface: Temple pews in Thailand flipped over a year after a storm surge carried them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the temple-and-pews string as one, giving SWEPTAW; in a down clue 'up' is the natural reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried off by a rush of water is the literal sense of the phrase.

clue.text: I met Presley dancing (after a fashion)

indicators.note: dancing sets the letters moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting Elvis Presley and dancing, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fashion' looks like an idiom for 'not very well', but 'after' is a link word and 'a fashion' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The neoclassical mode of dress and decor of Napoleon's France was a fashion of its day.

clue.text: Church land ahead of the curve?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
a bend is a curve

explanation.surface: A church plans its land use ahead of the curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral canon's stipend came from a portion of church estate, and the term also covers that property.

clue.text: Scarf got pinched from Latin American city

indicators.note: pinched from says the word got is stolen out of the city's name

parts.note: Bogota is the capital of Colombia

explanation.surface: A scarf was stolen from someone in a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is used twice over: taken as written, it is the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A long fluffy wrap of feathers or fur worn round the neck is a type of scarf.

clue.text: Laurel, Hardy finally getting rebate sorted out

indicators.note: getting says the scrambled letters receive the last letter of Hardy inside them
sorted out says the letters of rebate are rearranged
finally says only the last letter of Hardy is used

explanation.surface: Laurel and Hardy finally get their tax rebate sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel, Hardy' reads as the comedy duo, but Laurel is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet bay, whose leaves flavour stews, is the Mediterranean laurel tree.

clue.text: "Some cream, Erica?" "Nope; just black coffee."

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A host offers Erica cream; she declines and takes her coffee black.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso diluted with hot water, served without milk, is a style of plain dark coffee.

clue.text: Dramatist nursed in retirement by Edith Nesbit

indicators.note: in retirement says the held letters go backwards, withdrawing
nursed says the letters are held within the author's name

explanation.surface: A playwright was looked after in old age by the children's author Edith Nesbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses NESBI, which sits inside 'Edith Nesbit'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian author of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler was a playwright.

clue.text: See 15
Twice America grasped the head of Russian Bear

indicators.note: grasped says the doubled piece holds the Russian letter
Twice says the America abbreviation is written two times

parts.note: US is short for United States, America

indicators.note: the head of means the first letter of Russian

explanation.surface: America twice grasped the leader of Russia, the Russian bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursus is the Latin genus name for the bear family's typical members, such as the brown bear.

clue.text: Blue releasing record in fancy packaging

indicators.note: releasing says the record letters are let go

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling low, depressed
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A sad musician releases a record in a fancy sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing record' looks like issuing an album but means removing EP.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or goods presented with garnish or trim are decked out, given an attractive finish.

clue.text: Not very bright, I'm invested in obsolete currency

indicators.note: invested in says the I goes inside the old currency abbreviation

parts.note: DM is the Deutschmark, Germany's currency until the euro replaced it
I am, referring to oneself, gives the single letter I; the clue says this I is what goes in

explanation.surface: An investor admits to foolishly putting money into a defunct currency.
explanation.walkthrough: DM, the Deutschmark, was replaced by the euro in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a dull light or, figuratively, a slow-witted person.

clue.text: Be employed in sex trade at the lowest price?

indicators.note: in says the employment piece goes inside the other letters
trade means exchange, so the letters of sex swap places

parts.note: to be employed is to work

explanation.surface: A question about working in the sex industry at bargain rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade' gives EXS from 'sex'; the question mark flags that 'sex trade' is surface only. Ex-works is a commercial pricing term.
explanation.definitionFit: A price quoted at the factory gate excludes delivery and so is the cheapest basis for goods.

clue.text: Managed to cook — bottled gas

indicators.note: bottled says the cooking piece is held inside

parts.note: managed a business means ran it
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: Someone managed to cook with bottled gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive noble element that is gaseous at room temperature.

clue.text: Green favourite up north pushes May out

indicators.note: out says the letters are knocked out of place and reordered

explanation.surface: A popular figure in the Green party in the north pushes Theresa May out.
explanation.walkthrough: A bright green side dish of mashed marrowfat peas, a staple of northern English chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: This green side dish is especially popular in northern England, served with fish and chips.
